text.tspan: MEAN copies packed [T, H] as fp16 and reduces with MeanPool on the host.
Destagger of a device fp32 sum (to(fp16) then convert) is garbage (torch-spyre#2971). index_add_ (#3507) would let the reduce stay on the card.

· The metadata always describes the real batch, so no
padded row is ever pooled.
· Padding the body is safe: each layer treats every
token row on its own.
Pack the ragged flat list into a rectangle, so every
shape is fixed at compile time.
Needed because an offset computed from data does not
lower under compilation (torch-spyre#3508) — exactly
the arithmetic that flash relies on.
Eager tolerates it; compiled mode, our target, does not.
· build an additive mask [S, 1, L, L] marking padding
and cross-request slots
· build three index lists, then gather Q / K / V into
[S, H, L, D]
· one fused SDPA kernel per (S, L), then gather the
results back out
Shape axes: T for the body, (S, L) for attention.
Two sets of buckets to warm.
Costs: the mask grows with L², plus index lists and a
barrier per gather.
Works today. This is the current implementation.
Never materialise the rectangle.
Each block of queries reads its request's offset from
the metadata at runtime, and works directly on the flat
list, carrying a running softmax maximum and sum.
That is the online-softmax structure the Spyre decoder
already uses over KV pages.
· no [S, 1, L, L] mask; request boundaries are the offsets
· no gather_pack / gather_unpack; the kernel reads the
flat list directly
· no per-layer index lists, so no per-gather barriers
Shape axis: block count, bucketed like the decoder's
page loop. L disappears.
Both upstream backends already work this way, neither
padding into a rectangle.
Flash attention consumes the flat list with
cu_seqlens_q = query_start_loc, and the CPU backend
passes query[:num_actual_tokens] to a C++ kernel.
· the second shape axis collapses; bucket T and a block count,
much closer to upstream's single axis
· the batch-shape tables box disappears, and with it the
per-layer rebuild problem and its barriers
· gather_pack / SDPA / gather_unpack collapse into one
blocked-attention kernel
· the mask's L² growth at long prompts disappears, today's
largest untested risk
Open question:
whether a Spyre kernel can do the runtime
offset arithmetic this depends on. If it cannot, the block
count stays bucketed.
Everything else holds either way: padding seam, unpadded
metadata, warmup, compilation mode.
